**Linear SSA with implicit versioning** (structured code and CC region calls): a `wire`/`wire[N]` value is produced once and consumed once; mode `in` consumes and re-produces a successor of the same name; `consume` consumes; `produce` creates; a name is not used after `consume`.
**Regions are threaded the same way.** **Indexed operand** `w[i]` (literal i) borrows wire i for one instruction.

**Disjointness.** The wire operands of one instruction are pairwise distinct; **every wire of the effective control context is distinct from every target and from every consumed or produced operand** of an instruction executed under it (so `qpred p; x p` is ill-formed); a predicate wire is not modified between its push and its matching pop; a `qif`/`qloop … while` selector is not modified inside its arms or body.
A region's interface bundles and regions are pairwise disjoint.

**Per-opcode operand schema** (§4.8): every opcode has a tier set, a fixed arity, operand kinds and a result type; results are written first (`w = op a b`), modes are never written, and **result types that are not determined by the operands are written as a suffix** (`r = const.i32 5`, `r = zext.i64 a`, `r = trunc.i8 a`, `r = ptrtoint.i64 p`, `p = inttoptr a`).

Width rules: `binop`/`icmp` operands equal width; `select` arms equal width; `zext`/`sext` strictly widen, `trunc` strictly narrows; `load.iN` and `lift.load.iN` require N ∈ {8, 16, …, 128}; `measure` of `qreg[n]` with n ≤ 128 yields `in`; signed division truncates toward zero.

**Lifted width rules** (suite F; a mismatch is ill-formed, never a truncation or an extension). Every address operand (`a` of `lift.load`/ `lift.store`, `p` of `lift.boundscheck`/`lift.free`) and every address result (`w` of `lift.addr`/`lift.alloc`) is `reg[ptr_width]`; the length `n` of `lift.alloc`/`lift.boundscheck` is a location of any width or a literal in [0, 2^ptr_width); `inrange` and every prospective sum are computed at width max(widths of the operands involved) + 1 with no wrap.
The destination of `lift.label` and the operand of `qjumpr` have any width N with 2^N > n (the index-space size).

`lift.call` arguments have exactly the callee's parameter widths and its destination the callee's result width; `lift.ret v` has the containing lproc's result width; `lift.oracle_call`/`lift.oracle_uncall`/`lift.perm_call` operands have exactly the callee signature widths, and `mem` operands name caller regions whose `[A,W]` equal the callee's and whose role is `in` for an `in` slot (an `in` region is never passed to a `mut` slot); `fault C` and `lift.faultif p C` require the literal C < 2^F; the width rules above for `binop`, `icmp`, `select`, `zext`, `sext`, `trunc` apply verbatim to their `lift.*` counterparts; the destinations of one `lift.parmov` are pairwise distinct.
**Quantum registers in CC.** `qreg[n]` names n device-resident wires.
A handle is in exactly one state: **live**, **viewed** (one slice of it is live) or **consumed**; an instruction whose precondition fails is a CC trap.
**Handle transitions:**
`q = qreg.new cls n` | – | q live, clean
`qreg.free q` | q live, not a view, clean on every basis configuration (a simulator checks and reports `E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN`; hardware records a program error in the run) | q consumed

`q2 = qreg.slice q lo len` | q live, not a view, lo + len ≤ n | q2 live (wires [lo, lo+len) of q), q viewed; q2 MUST be the operand of exactly one region call and of nothing else; after that call q2 is consumed and q is live again; any use of q while viewed is ill-formed (suite F)
`q = qreg.concat q1 q2` | q1, q2 live, not views | q1, q2 consumed; q live over the wires of q1 then q2
region call (§4.7) with q as operand | q live (a view included) | q unchanged
`r = measure q` | q live, not a view | q consumed, its wires released
reversal of a `qreg.*` frame (§7.4, §10) | – | the handle states before that frame.
A `measure` frame is **never reversed**: a segment containing one cannot be uncalled (§7.4) and a run containing one is not reversible (§10)
**Binding**: a `qreg[n]` argument fills a `wire[n]` slot bit for bit (bit 0 ↔ wire 0); it fills a `region[A,W]` slot iff n = 2^A·W with cell i = bits [iW, (i+1)W).

statements.text: Branch and call targets are labels; `w = lift.label ^b` is the only way a location obtains an index value; executors MAY re-index dispatch extensionally **provided every label value observable through `lift.label` keeps its canonical numeric value**.
**Terminators**: `qjump qbranch qjumpr lift. ret lift.retval fault`; every block ends in one; no label names HALT; **only `lift.retval` reaches HALT with success**.

**Row classes.** Each §4.2 row is an **assignment** (A: written locations/cells receive values computed out of place into frame slots `disp_j`, then exchanged in, so `disp_j` retains the displaced old value), a **direct** row (D: a controlled permutation in place), or **mixed** (A+D) with an explicit ordered list of **elementary sub-operations** printed in §3.7.
**Slot kinds.** An **assignment slot** receives a value computed out of place and is then exchanged with its destination (it retains the displaced old value).
A **capture slot** receives a value computed out of place and is never exchanged (it retains that value as history: the arguments of `lift.call`).
The **delivery slot** of `lift.ret` is a capture slot that is subsequently exchanged, under a condition, with the destination location.

Rows with a **flag** compute it into `frame.flag` from the old state before any effect; rows with a data-dependent successor compute it into `frame. succ` before any effect; conditional-fault rows perform `faulted ^= flag`, `code ^= flag·C` after their other effects.

**Dispatch.** `at_k = (pc == k)` for k = 0..n into clean scratch.

**D row**: its sub-operations in reverse order, each by its own inverse (`lift.perm_call` by the callee's adjoint; XORs, controlled flips and exchanges by themselves).

**A row**: exchange every assignment slot back with its destination **in the reverse of the forward exchange order** (the forward order is the row's listed slot order; every destination address, forward and inverse, is evaluated from the state current at that exchange, so an indexed destination such as `alloctab[atop]` is addressed with the counter value that the earlier inverse exchanges have already restored), then **uncompute every slot from the restored old state** (the same out-of-place computation, applied again as XOR, clears it).

**A+D row**: **the exact reverse of its complete §3.7 sub-operation list**, each elementary sub-operation inverted at its reversed position: a direct sub-operation by its own inverse; an assignment sub-operation by exchanging its slot back and then uncomputing the slot; a capture sub-operation by uncomputing the slot (its source has been restored by the sub-operations already undone); the delivery sub-operation by the same conditional exchanges.

**Every address and condition is evaluated from the state current at that position of the inverse** (so the `lift.ret` stack addresses and delivery condition use the callee `fp` restored one position earlier, and the `lift.call` record base uses the restored `sp`); §3.7 prints both inverse lists.
Finally uncompute `frame_t.succ` and `frame_t.flag` from the restored old state.

**C3 record**: `stack[sp] ^= k+1` (ret index), `stack[sp+1] ^= fp`, `stack[sp+2] ^= id(w)` (direct XORs into clean cells);

To clear `fr'`, the producer emits `lift.oracle_uncall @o` with the same token, callee, `ins` and `mem` values (no intervening row writes those locations or cells: suite F) and the successor versions of `tgt` and `fr'`; the pair shares a dynamic invocation identity.
Alternatively `fr'` is retained until the prefix reversal.
**Requirement.** A region's completed operation equals its declared operation ⊗ identity on every borrowed bundle and on any external system entangled with it.

**Rule (suite F).** Borrowed wires (set B) are touched (as control or target) only inside **borrow frames**: maximal contiguous permutation- only subcircuits from the first to the last instruction touching B.

The frame's realised permutation P_F on its wires MUST factor as `P_F = P' ⊗ I_B`, established by a T3 claim over the frame's full domain (exhaustive, or a library certificate, §12 `borrow_frames`) or **structurally by the translation lemma**: the frame is `V; W; V⁻¹; W` where
(i) every gate of V is an X-family flip (`x cx ccx mcx`) whose **target is in B** and whose **controls are all in a set X with X ∩ B = ∅**; V touches no other wire; hence V maps b ↦ b ⊕ v(X);
(ii) every gate of W is an X-family flip whose **target is outside X, outside B, and outside the set of all controls of W** (as sets, over the whole of W), and W writes no wire of X;
(iii) every gate of W has **at most one control in B**;
(iv) V⁻¹ is the exact reverse sequence of V; no `swap` appears in the frame.
Then W's effect is affine in b, the net map is t ⊕= Σ_g c_g(Y)·v_{j(g)}(X), independent of b, and b is restored (the dirty-ancilla MCX pattern).

Suite F contains the negative tests `cx b y; cx y z; cx b y` (V;W;V⁻¹), `V = cx b2 b1, W = cx b1 t` (b2 ∈ B, violates X ∩ B = ∅), `V = cx b x` (target outside B), and `W = swap y z; cx b y` (swap excluded).
Oracles are one frame verified by their own T3 claim over D.
Inlining, structure recovery, dispatch re-indexing and simplification MUST produce on every x ∈ D the same final interface tuple as §5.2's construction on the reference body (T6).
Every workspace bundle version, location version and cell version has provenance `perm` (computed by permutation gates from its **dependency set** S of versions) or `other`.

non-diagonal gate on u | u: other; closes the window of every value whose S contains u

A perm value g with set S is **in its window** from its computation until the first of: a non-diagonal gate on a wire in S or in g; a version advance of a cell in S; a non-permutation action call touching a wire in S; a permutation change to a wire in S not undone before g's cleanup.
Each cleanup is bound to its exact computing sequence and requires the versions that sequence read to be current.
Every perm value MUST be cleaned within its window and before its region exits; otherwise the region is **ill-formed** (closed-window measurement-based cleanup is not admitted).
`other` values are released only by the adjoint of the sequence that produced them.

Cleaning g within its window returns g's wires to |0⟩ and factorises them from the remaining state; diagonal uses of g or of its dependencies have applied the corresponding diagonal phases to the remainder, which is part of the program's declared semantics.

Every cleanup in this version is **unitary**: realisation `reverse` (the adjoint of g's exact computing sequence, §6.2) or `recompute` (legal for `perm` values only: recompute g into a fresh clean bundle by the same sequence, `qxor` it into g's wires, uncompute the fresh bundle by the adjoint).

**Measurement-based cleanup is not admitted in sched/ cert 0.8**: a schedule naming any other realisation is invalid, the target capability `mbu` is reserved and MUST be `false`, and no cleanup produces a `channel` claim. *(non-normative)* The fixup after an X-basis measurement of g with outcome m is the phase (−1)^{m·g(x)}, a function of g's computing sequence and not of the target; its normative form, its controlled variant and its certificate kind are deferred (§17 item 6; default: unitary cleanup).

Schedules and certificate cleanup entries are keyed by `(region hash, variant, inherited control count)`; a region reachable under a non-empty control context MUST have a cleanup schedule for that key.

statements.text: `layout` partitions the address space: a **null region** `[0, null_size)` never allocated (null_size ≥ 1); globals at fixed bases with images; the heap `[heap_base, heap_base + heap_limit_max)`, all disjoint, `heap_base + heap_limit_max ≤ 2^ptr_ width`, and the number of globals ≤ 2^A_tab, all validated at load.

`p = alloc n` **fails before any mutation** when bump + max(n, 1) > heap_base + heap_limit_max or the table holds 2^A_tab entries (CC trap / R fault `FAULT_BUDGET_HEAP`); otherwise it returns the bump pointer, records `(base, size = n, live = 1, pinned = 0)` and advances by `max(n, 1)`; globals have pre-entered pinned live entries; an access is valid iff its whole byte range lies in one live entry; `free p` marks the unique live entry with base p dead (pinned entries cannot be freed; no such entry: CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_MEMFAULT`); storage is never reclaimed.
Initial state: bump = `heap_base`, table = the pre-entries in layout order, memory zero except images.
`mem` has 2^H byte cells (H ≤ ptr_width); `alloctab` 2^A_tab entries `(base, size, live, pinned)`; the stack 2^S_cells cells.

The `layout` fixes `null_size`, each global's base and image, `heap_base`, `heap_ limit_max`, and for each **interface region** of the oracle (W = 8 required) a base address; all ranges disjoint and within `[0, 2^H)`, and for every oracle the number of pre-entries (globals plus its interface regions) ≤ 2^A_tab, checked at load.
`lift.load`/`lift.store` dispatch by address range to `mem` or to the mapped interface region (role `in` preserved by the construction).

**Pure frames.** A frame is **pure** iff it belongs to `br` or to a defining instruction among `const`, the binops, `udiv..srem`, `icmp`, `select`, `zext sext trunc`, `ptrtoint inttoptr`, `load`: it changes only the set of instances.
Every other frame (`store alloc free call ret uncall trap effect hostcall qreg.* measure`, region calls, fault records) is impure.

**History traversal** (the one reversal procedure, used by segment `uncall` and by whole-run reversal). A range of frames is **reversed** by visiting its frames in LIFO order; a frame already marked reversed and an `uncall` frame are **skipped**; every other frame is undone by its row of the table above and then marked reversed.
Reversed frames stay in the history, marked, and are never undone again (a reversed segment's `uncall` marker is retired with it).
**Segment uncall** (`uncall @f (args) (results)`).
Let S be the most recent completed call segment of the history (a `call` frame, its matching `ret` frame and every frame between them).

The `uncall` is legal iff S is a call of `@f`, S's recorded boundary argument and result values equal the operand values, **every frame after S is pure**, and S contains, at any nesting depth, **no `measure` frame** and no `qreg. free` frame whose cleanliness was not verified (hardware, §17 item 14); otherwise it is a CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_TRAP` and changes nothing.

Execution reverses S by the history traversal (nested segments are undone; nested segments already cancelled by an inner `uncall`, and that inner `uncall` frame, are skipped), and pushes an `uncall` frame naming S.
The instances defined inside S no longer exist; using such a name before it is redefined is a CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_TRAP`.

**Whole-run reversal** (§10) is the history traversal over the whole history: S's effects on memory, the allocation table, devices and handles were undone by the `uncall`, and the frames between S and the `uncall` are pure, so at the `uncall` frame every component except the retained instances already equals its value before S.
T4 is stated over these frames. *(non-normative)* S is never re-executed and never redone; the compute–copy–`uncall` idiom derives what it keeps through pure instructions before the `uncall`.
Suite A contains: `f` calls `g`, uncalls `g`, returns; `g` performs one `clock.read`; `call f; uncall f` leaves the clock at its entry value; and `uncall` of a segment that measured is a trap.

```

  (2) "ptr_width=" INT
  (3) the JCS signature
  (4) the canonical function bytes (with reference tokens replaced, below); for a data symbol: its data line NAME SP HEX
  (5a) for every data entry in the closure set, sorted by name bytewise:        "data " NAME " " HEX

  (5c) for an R/CC function, for every device model and service it uses, sorted: "device " <name> " " <JCS entry>

```
**Closure set**, by symbol kind.

**Oracle**: **all** `layout` leaves of the object except `interface_regions` entries of other oracles (every global's pre-entry affects its allocation faults), its own `interface_ regions.<oracle>.*` leaves, and every data image those leaves name.
**Lproc**: the leaves and images of every global `@g` it names in `lift. addr`.
**Action / permutation action**: no layout leaves; the `@image` of each `qregion` is an ordinary symbol reference (replaced in part (4), listed in part (6)).
**CC / R function**: all `layout` leaves, every data image they name, and in (5c) every device model and `hostcall` service it uses.
**Data symbol**: parts (5)–(6) are empty.

A layout leaf is a scalar or an object at the deepest level the schema lists (`globals. <name>` and `interface_regions.<oracle>.<region>` are leaves; `ptr_ width`, `H`, … are leaves); a scalar's JCS value is its decimal text.

**Globals are data symbols**: every global `g` in `layout.globals` MUST have `image` = `g` and the object MUST define a `data` symbol named `g` of that size, so the token `@g` in `lift.addr` is both the global and a symbol reference (replaced by the data symbol's hash; the global's `base` and `size` enter through the layout leaf).
An `@name` naming an interface region (in `lift.addr`) is not a symbol reference and is left unchanged.

**Reference replacement**: in parts (4)–(5) every `@name` symbol-reference token is replaced by `@` followed by the referenced symbol's 64-hex hash (the symbol's own name in its header line is a definition, not a reference, and is left unchanged); the **interface hash** uses interface hashes of defined symbols and `SHA-256(name ‖ 0x00 ‖ JCS signature)` (hex) for unresolved imports; the **closure hash** uses closure hashes.

statements.text: **Model.** A run executes a device CC entry; the host passes classical arguments, register ids and the entropy tape, receives classical results, fault codes and declared measurements; host services are reached by `hostcall`.

**Positional binding**: argument i of `bennett_ run` binds to parameter i of the entry's signature: `INT(width, bytes)` to `iN` with width = N (else `E_ARG`), `F64` to `f64`, `QREG` to `qreg[n]` with the register's n, `TOKEN` to `token`.
Arguments and the entropy tape are **copied** at `bennett_run`; the caller may free its buffers afterwards.
Tokens are scoped to the program and destroyed at unload.
Accessor-returned pointers are valid until the owning object is freed.
`bennett_unload` with a run not CLOSED: `E_INVALID_STATE`.

**Invocation tree.** A run record is a tree (CC segments, R calls, Q calls); an R call's subtree is owned by its R history; `bennett_reverse` reverses post-order: CC segments by their run history, R calls by LIFO reversal of their history (§7.4, reversed segments and `uncall` frames skipped), top-level Q calls by re-application / adjoint.

**States.** `CREATED → RUNNING → (SUSPENDED ⇄ RUNNING) → (HOST_REQUEST ⇄ RUNNING) → COMPLETED | FAILED`; `COMPLETED → REVERSED`; any of `COMPLETED/FAILED/REVERSED → CLOSED` (`bennett_run_close` releases the record; register ids created by the run remain valid unless measured or freed).
A run owns the registers and memory it touches exclusively while not CLOSED.
**Reverse eligibility**: `COMPLETED`; no `measure`; no register it touched has been prepared, freed, sliced or used by another run since; else `E_NOT_REVERSIBLE`.

`bennett_qreg_prepare` and `bennett_ qreg_free` require a clean register (`E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN` otherwise); there is no reset and no trace-out: a register in unknown state is released by a `measure` inside a run, which consumes its handle (§3.3).

**Results.** `bennett_result_get` writes value i and sets `*kind` and `*width`: `INT` as ⌈N/8⌉ little-endian bytes, `*width` = N; `F64` as the 8 IEEE 754 binary64 little-endian bytes, `*width` = 64; `QREG` and `TOKEN` as the 8-byte little-endian id, `*width` = 64.
A `cap` smaller than that byte count is `E_ARG` and nothing is written.
Fault records are read by `bennett_result_nfaults` / `bennett_result_fault` (codes of §5.4, in order of occurrence; a `COMPLETED` run has none, a `FAILED` run has at least one and exposes no values).

**Waiting.** `bennett_wait` blocks until the run leaves `RUNNING` and returns `OK` with exactly one outcome: `HOST_REQUEST` (`*request_out` set, `*result_out` NULL; `bennett_reply` answers it and the run is `RUNNING` again) or `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` (`*result_out` set, `*request_ out` NULL).
Waiting on a `SUSPENDED`, `REVERSED` or `CLOSED` run is `E_ INVALID_STATE`.

**`hostcall`.** `rlen = hostcall service ptr len`: `[ptr, ptr + len)` MUST lie in one live allocation (else CC trap and no request is made); those bytes are copied into the request; the run enters `HOST_REQUEST`; the reply payload is written to `[ptr, ptr + min(len, reply length))` and `rlen` = the full reply length (so truncation is detectable); the frame records the request bytes, the overwritten bytes and the reply bytes.
Every `service` is declared in `devices.services`; an undeclared one is a load error.

**Tape.** `bennett_tape_next` yields each `effect` in tape order; `args` holds the operation's operands in the order of §7.3, each an unsigned 64-bit little-endian field (pointers zero-extended from `ptr_width`), so `*alen` = 8 × arity.
**Generated operations and the expansion library.** Every row and instruction expands into **generated operations** (gates, allocations, releases).
Above gate level the order is fixed by §3.6, §4.2, §4.5–§4.6 and §5.2 (dispatch comparators k = 0..n in index order; a row's sub-operations in listed order; successor XORs; commit; cleanup).

Below that level (the gate decomposition of comparators, adders, multiplexers, `inrange` scans and their scratch) the expansion is defined by an **expansion library**: a versioned document, identified in the schedule's `bindings.expansion` as `{ "name", "version", "hash" }`, that lists for every row kind and every instruction its generated operations in order, with their **ordinals**, scratch identities and the subset it marks removable, and that is extensionally equal to the reference (§5.7, T6).
A consumer that does not implement the bound library rejects the schedule (`E_SCHEDULE_INFEASIBLE`); two consumers implementing it execute and charge the same operation set.
`bennett-isa-spec` publishes the reference library `ref` (§17 item 7).

statements.text: §5.7 transformations under a schedule MUST keep the ordinals of the operations they keep and MAY remove only operations the library marks removable.
**Schedule document** (JCS):

```
  { "bindings": { "closure_hash", "target_hash", "region", "variant", "inherited_controls", "budget": [B,heap,stack,depth],
                  "params_hash", "epsilon", "expansion": { "name", "version", "hash" }, "scheduler": { "name", "version" } },
    "entries": [ { "path": [ { "symbol": hex, "point": "<block>:<ordinal>", "iteration": [n, …] | "*" }, … ],
                   "step": n | "*",  "phase": "fwd" | "rev" | "*",  "generated": n | "*",
                   "kind": "cleanup" | "gate" | "alloc" | "start",
                   "cleanup": { "realisation": "reverse" | "recompute" },
                   "gate":    { "realisation": "native" | "<scheme name>", "epsilon_share": decimal },
                   "alloc":   { "class": "<cls>" },           /* a concrete class; "any" is not allowed in a schedule */
                   "start":   { "time": decimal } } ] }
```

**Matching.** Every generated operation has an **invocation chain**: the program points of the region calls, `lift.call`s and `lift.oracle_call`s that led to it, outermost first, ending in its own point.

`path` matches an operation iff it is a **prefix** of that chain, element by element: `symbol` and `point` equal, and `iteration` either `*` or equal to the vector of 0-based dynamic repetition counts of the `qloop`s enclosing that point (outermost first; its length is the point's loop nesting depth, `[]` outside every loop).

`step` is the forward machine step t ∈ 1..B of an oracle-generated operation (`phase: rev` denotes the inverse of step t; both are per invocation level, so a nested oracle's step is selected by a path element for the nested call); `generated` is the ordinal within the row's expansion in the bound library.

**Specificity** is the lexicographic tuple (path length, number of non-`*` iterations, step non-`*`, phase non-`*`, generated non-`*`); an entry applies to a generated operation iff all its selectors match; among matching entries the unique maximal one applies; **two incomparable maximal matching entries make the schedule invalid** (document order is never significant).
Selectors are resolved independently per `kind`.

Defaults for uncovered operations: `reverse`; `native` if the gate matches a `gates` entry, else the first matching scheme; class = the first class declared in the target's `classes` object (JCS order) that has capacity for it; sequential timing in generated order.
**Timing**: a `start` time MUST be ≥ the end of every operation the operation depends on (data, wire lifetime, region cell version, effect order); an entry violating this makes the schedule invalid.
**Obligations**: satisfy §6; respect capacity; report every resource; be reproducible from the request plus scheduler version.
A consumer validates every binding and every path against the object and executes verbatim or rejects (`E_SCHEDULE_ INFEASIBLE`).

`structural` | `{ "rule": "translation_lemma" \| "inverse_pair_library" \| "adjoint_table", "subclaims": [indices], "witness": … }`; for `translation_lemma`: `{ "V": [points], "W": [points], "X": [wires], "B": [wires], "frame": [first point, last point] }`; for `inverse_pair_library`: `{ "library_closure_hash", "claim_index" }`; for `adjoint_table`: `{}` | check the rule's side conditions syntactically against the object and the subclaims' results

`numerical` | `{ "subject": { "closure_hash", "variant", "inherited_controls", "schedule_hash" }, "metric": "operator_norm", "precision_bits": n, "bound": decimal }` | **checker-computed, for every invocation context of the subject** (below): build the realised unitary U of that invocation (the region's realisation under the root schedule at that path, with its resolved classical arguments, budget, epsilon shares and cleanup choices, and `inherited_controls` control wires prepended) and the reference unitary V (the region's §5.3 semantics with the same arguments, controlled on the same wires) at the subject's signature widths in interval arithmetic at `precision_bits` (basis order = allocation order, controls first), form interval enclosures of `V†U − I` entrywise, derive the operator-norm bound as the Frobenius-norm upper bound in interval arithmetic, and verify it is ≤ `bound`; the claim holds iff it holds for every context

`channel` | `{ "subject": as above, "metric": "diamond", "precision_bits", "bound", "dual": [ { "Y": interval Hermitian matrix, "mu": decimal } … ] }` | for every invocation context of the subject, in enumeration order, verify its dual witness for the **diamond-norm SDP** below in interval arithmetic and `mu` ≤ `bound` (one witness per context; too few witnesses: reject)

**Invocation contexts.** A subject denotes the set of invocations of the region `closure_hash`, with the given `variant` and `inherited_ controls`, in the root schedule `schedule_hash`: every path of that schedule's region tree reaching the region, with the classical arguments, budget, `epsilon_share`s and cleanup realisations resolved at that path.
Contexts are enumerated in path order (the schedule's `entries` paths sorted bytewise as JCS).
Every claim bound and every `error` entry (§12.3) is a **common upper bound over all contexts** of its key; the multiplicity composition of §12.3 is sound for that reason.
**Diamond-norm SDP** (Watrous, *Theory of Computing* 5 (2009), §4; the Hermiticity-preserving simplification).
Let Φ = Φ_real − Φ_ref be the difference of the subject's realised channel and the reference channel (both on the subject's interface, controls included), d_in = d_out = d the dimension.
The **Choi matrix** is J(Φ) = Σ_{i,j} |i⟩⟨j| ⊗ Φ(|i⟩⟨j|) (input factor first, output factor second, computational basis in allocation order, **unnormalised**).
The witness is a Hermitian Y of dimension d² and a decimal mu.

The checker accepts iff, with every matrix entry an interval and every test rigorous (an inconclusive test rejects): Y − J(Φ) ⪰ 0, Y + J(Φ) ⪰ 0, mu·I − Tr_out(Y) ⪰ 0 (partial trace over the output factor), and mu ≤ `bound`; then ‖Φ‖◇ ≤ mu (the dual of Watrous's SDP with Y₀ = Y₁ = Y; this is the diamond norm itself, not half of it).
Encoding: `Y` is a row-major array of entries `[re_lo, re_ hi, im_lo, im_hi]` (decimal strings).

**Positivity test.** The checker proves each of the three matrices **positive definite** by an interval Cholesky (or Hermitian LDL†) factorisation in which the interval lower bound of every pivot is strictly positive, and rejects otherwise; no other test is admitted (nonnegative leading principal minors do not imply positive semidefiniteness: diag(0, −1)).

Producers make witnesses strictly feasible by replacing Y with Y + δI and mu with mu′ = mu + δ·(d + 1) for a small rational δ > 0 (any mu′ > mu + δ·d suffices): then Y ± J(Φ) ⪰ δI ≻ 0 and, since Tr_out(Y + δI) = Tr_out(Y) + δ·d·I, mu′·I − Tr_out(Y + δI) ⪰ δI ≻ 0; ‖Φ‖◇ ≤ mu′, which MUST be ≤ `bound`.

**Interval arithmetic** at `precision_bits` means every operation rounds outward to `precision_bits`-bit binary rationals; transcendental entries (`rx ry rz`) are enclosed by a Taylor series with the Lagrange remainder bound (§17 item 8 fixes the term count).
The subject's `schedule_hash` is required: an executable claim names the realisation it is about.

**Sampling.** For each domain component with range size R = hi − lo + 1, assemble m = ⌈⌈log₂ R⌉/64⌉ consecutive generator words (least-significant word first) into an integer, reduce modulo 2^⌈log₂ R⌉, reject and redraw if ≥ R, add `lo`; components are consumed in enumeration order.

A controlled unitary variant requires a `numerical` claim; an ε > 0 realisation compared as a channel requires a `channel` claim.
Executable claims (`numerical`, `channel`, `exhaustive` with `expected: "oracle"`) bind to `schedule_hash` through their subject.

statements.text: Executes an oracle's reference body per basis configuration: locations and cells are bit-vectors, pseudo-locations read-only, predication is `if`, each §4.2 row is its classical function (including the inherent `inrange` check of loads and stores, the activation records of §3.7, the `alloctab` and stack arrays), `fault` records the code and halts, `lift. retval` halts with success and `f(x) = result_val`, the step counter counts executed rows, counters are unbounded integers.
It **defines** F_B and the budget unit and rejects any body that executes a non-permutation gate.
The state of a Q region is a vector in ⊗ over live wires in allocation order (bundles little-endian).

`qalloc` tensors |0⟩; `qfree` removes clean factors; `qborrow` introduces a factor in unknown state possibly entangled with a reference system R, and the region's operation must be U ⊗ I on it (§5.6); gates act by §4.4 under the active predicate; `measure` (CC) is the projective computational-basis measurement with Born probabilities, consuming the wires.
**T1 (totality).** For every well-formed oracle, budget and x ∈ D the reference interpreter halts within B + 1 rows and F_B(x) is unique.

**T2 (prefix reversal).** For every executor whose realisation is a composition of ε = 0 permutation gates implementing §5.2 steps 1–4 with the inverse step of §3.6, on every x ∈ D every non-interface wire is clean after step 4 and borrowed bundles hold their initial values.
**T3 (permutation theorem).** If the realised unitary V of a circuit on span(D) is a permutation matrix and the final basis tuple equals P(x) for every x ∈ D, then V|span(D) = P.

**T4 (round trip).** For every finite valid CC/R trace with retained run history and tapes, LIFO reversal per §7.4 restores the classical environment, memory, allocation table, device-model state and history to entry values; observed external events are not retracted.

**T6 (executor agreement).** Two executors conforming to §3–§7 on one target with the same schedule produce on every x ∈ D the same final tuple for every oracle (exact) and, for every action with `operator_ norm` inclusive bounds e₁, e₂, unitaries within e₁ + e₂ in operator norm; for channels, diamond bounds d₁ + d₂.

A | Executor | classical ISA; run history and LIFO reversal with loops, recursion, effects, segment `uncall` (impure suffix traps; nested `uncall` inside an uncalled segment; `uncall` over a `measure` traps), `hostcall`, `qreg.*`, fault records (T4)

B | Executor | oracle totality and prefix reversal: every fault code; B = 0; boundary halts; `lift.call`/`lift.ret` recursion with argument capture; one forward `lift.call` and one forward `lift.ret` step of a recursive call each followed by its inverse (§3.7); stack exhaustion (`sp + R_f > stack_limit`); matched `lift.oracle_uncall`; interface regions restored; pre-entries; `lift.free` on pinned entries; inherent load/store checks

C | Executor, Producer | T3 over full D at exhaustive widths for oracles, permutation actions, `qinplace` pairs, borrow frames; T6 agreement among VM, specialiser, transformed forms and the reference interpreter; the §16.3 examples as normative test vectors, including the stack-capacity boundary of example 2
D | Executor | channel and unitary comparison for ε > 0 realisations; controlled-interference tests; checker-computed bounds; the diamond-norm SDP witness check of §12.1
E | Target author, Executor | JCS parsing; AST evaluation; matching; scheme expansion and correctness; aggregation from event lists; timing model; imports

F | Producer | versioning, disjointness incl. control context; operand schema; row classes and frame sizing; index-space flattening; terminators; name resolution; permutation-only oracles; §6 transfer and windows; adjoint table; translation lemma side conditions with the four negative tests; `in`-wire use; acyclic action graphs; grammar; schemas; envelope and hashes; linking; frame-descriptor live ranges
G | Launch | every §10 entry point, state transition, binding rule, ownership rule; HOST_REQUEST/reply; reverse eligibility and tree order
H | Scheduler | §6 validity; capacity; reproducibility; specificity resolution; verbatim execution; INFEASIBLE/UNSUPPORTED
UTF-8; LF line endings; one instruction per line; tokens separated by exactly one space; no trailing spaces; exactly one blank line before each `section` line and none elsewhere.

statements.text: Metadata lines are RFC 8785 canonical JSON objects.

```
  object    := header NL section*
  header    := "bennett-object" SP "isa=" VER SP "object=" VER SP "launch=" VER SP "sched=" VER SP "cert=" VER SP "coverage=" VER SP "target=" VER SP "ptr_width=" INT
  section   := NL "section" SP SECTNAME NL body
  SECTNAME  := "symbols" | "imports" | "functions" | "data" | "devices" | "layout" | "schedule" | "certificate" | "coverage"
  body      := jsonline | dataline* | function*
  jsonline  := JCS-canonical JSON object NL
  dataline  := NAME SP HEX NL
  function  := fhead NL regs? block+
  fhead     := ("fn" SP ("cc"|"r") | "oracle" | "action" | "perm_action" | "lproc") SP "@" NAME SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")"
               -- oracle: (in..) (tgt) (fault) (mem..) (args..) ; action: (mut..) (in..) (mem..) (args..) () ; lproc: (params..) (result) () () () ; fn: (params..) (results..) () () ()
  plist     := (param ("," SP param)*)?
  param     := NAME ":" type (SP ("in"|"mut"))?
  type      := "i" INT | "ptr" | "f64" | "token" | "wire" | "wire[" INT "]" | "reg[" INT "]" | "region[" INT "," INT "]" | "qreg[" INT "]"
  regs      := "regs" SP "{" SP (NAME ":" type ("," SP NAME ":" type)*)? SP "}" (SP "bounds" SP "{" INT ("," SP INT)* "}")? NL
  block     := "^" NAME "(" plist "):" NL instr+
  instr     := (lhs SP "=" SP)? OPCODE (SP operand)* (SP "{" NL instr+ "}" (SP "{" NL instr+ "}")?)? NL
  lhs       := NAME | "(" NAME ("," SP NAME)* ")"
  operand   := NAME | NAME "[" INT "]" | "@" NAME | "^" NAME ("(" (NAME ("," SP NAME)*)? ")")? | INT | FLOAT | STRING | "(" (NAME ("," SP NAME)*)? ")"
  OPCODE    := a mnemonic of §4 with its dotted suffix (§4.8 fixes operand count, kinds and result placement)
  VER       := INT "." INT
```

statements.text: `alloctab` starts with pinned entries (16,1) and (4096,16), `atop = 2`.

`@sum` resolves `n acc base` to its params and everything else to its own locations; its locations are `n acc base` (params), `r` (result name), then its nine `regs`: m′ = 13, **R_sum = 16 cells**; `@sum_db` reads `n` as a pseudo- location.
Input n performs n + 1 nested calls (the last at depth n + 1) and, the stack being monotonic, occupies 16(n + 1) stack cells.

With sufficient budget F_B(n) = (Σ_{i<n} db[i] mod 256, 0) for n ≤ 16 (n = 16 needs 272 cells, hence S_cells = 9 and `stack_limit ≥ 272`); for n > 16 the check at `p` faults `FAULT_UB_MEMFAULT` on the first out-of-range byte; with small B, `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS`; with `depth_limit ≤ n` or `stack_limit < 16(n + 1)`, `FAULT_BUDGET_DEPTH`.

Hashes by §9.2: `@zero` is a data symbol and the `zero` global's image; `@sum` is a one-member SCC (its self-reference is written `@$0`, its `@zero` reference is replaced by `@` + the `zero` hash, which is its only part-(6) line; its closure set is the `zero` global's leaf and image), so its envelope is exactly the bytes below, its `scc_hash` is their SHA-256 and its hash is SHA-256 of the ASCII `<scc_hash hex>:0`:

```

ptr_width=32
{"abi":"0.8","kind":"lproc","params":[8,8,32],"result":8,"tier":"q"}
lproc @sum (n:reg[8], acc:reg[8], base:reg[32]) (r:reg[8]) () () ()
regs { zp:reg[32], zv:reg[8], z:reg[1], one:reg[8], n2:reg[8], idx:reg[32], p:reg[32], v:reg[8], acc2:reg[8] }
^entry():
zp = lift.addr @7002ed5ea010907a0ae99065663f22fb7d18ca1d6cb171fed57e2594bd9367e6
lift.boundscheck zp 1
zv = lift.load.i8 zp
z = lift.icmp.eq n zv
qbranch z ^done ^more
^more():
one = lift.const.i8 1
n2 = lift.sub n one
idx = lift.zext.i32 n2
p = lift.add base idx
lift.boundscheck p 1
v = lift.load.i8 p
acc2 = lift.add acc v
r = lift.call @$0 (n2, acc2, base)
lift.ret r
```

`@sum_db`'s envelope includes every layout leaf, the `zero` image, `@` + the `sum` hash in place of `@sum`, and the `sum` hash as its part-(6) line (`@db` is an interface region, not a symbol):
Each item is one an implementer must decide to build; any decision is conformant provided two implementations agree on the default below until the item is revised.
Items 1–5 are asserted non-semantic.
**Binary encoding.** Default: none; §16 text is the only interchange form.
**Gate-name registry.** Default: the names of §4.4 only; an unknown gate name is a load error.
**Further device models.** Default: the four of §7.3; an `effect` on any other device is `FAULT_EFFECT_UNMODELLED`.
**Mechanisation of §14.** Default: none; the reference interpreter is the oracle.
**Memory layout of the opaque C objects.** Default: opaque; only the listed functions touch them.
